This page describes how `SimilaritySearchEngine.jl` is put together: its module map, the
engine type hierarchy that replaces name/enum-based dispatch with real Julia types, the
staging-vs-indexing split that lets a dense project decouple insertion from the expensive
graph-connection step, the concurrency model that lets searches run in parallel while
staying safe from concurrent inserts, and the RocksDB-column-families-plus-one-mmap-file
layout that makes persistence incremental instead of a single ever-growing blob.

## Module map

The package is five source files, four of them real submodules (`Schema`, `Project`,
`IndexEngine`, `Persistence`) plus `embedded.jl`, which defines `EmbeddedEngine` and the
top-level functions (`create_project`, `append_items!`, `search`, ...) directly in the
`SimilaritySearchEngine` module itself — the friendly surface a script actually calls.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    Schema["Schema<br/><small>MetadataRecord (_id, doc_id,<br/>keywords, refs), meta split</small>"]
    Project["Project<br/><small>ProjectManager, metadata CRUD</small>"]
    IndexEngine["IndexEngine<br/><small>AbstractSearchEngine hierarchy</small>"]
    Persistence["Persistence<br/><small>EngineStore, AdjacencyStore, ...</small>"]
    Embedded["embedded.jl<br/><small>EmbeddedEngine + top-level API</small>"]
    Caller(["Julia script, or<br/>SimilaritySearchServer"])

    Schema --> Project
    Schema --> Embedded
    Project --> Embedded
    IndexEngine --> Embedded
    Persistence --> Embedded
    Embedded --> Caller
```

`IndexEngine` and `Persistence` are deliberately independent of `Project`/`Schema` and of
each other: `IndexEngine` knows nothing about RocksDB (its persistence hook is a plain
`(index, sp, ep) -> nothing` callback), and `Persistence` knows nothing about metadata
schemas or search engines (it stores plain Julia values under string keys). `embedded.jl`
is the one place that wires all four together — every other module could, in principle,
be reused on its own.

`Schema`/`Project` have no per-project typed-field schema to declare anymore: every
project has exactly the same fixed-shape `Schema.MetadataRecord` (`_id`, `doc_id`,
`keywords`, `refs`) plus a free-form `meta` JSON blob for everything else appended with an
item — `_id` is the internal, sequential, always-present handle (the same id space the
engine's own vector/text store uses); `doc_id` is the caller's own external id, if any;
`keywords`/`refs` are the only two fields with a secondary index (`Project`'s fixed
`idx_keywords`/`idx_refs` column families), everything else lives in `meta`, looked up
straight from `Project`, never indexed.

## Engine type hierarchy

Every index kind (`SearchGraph`, `ExhaustiveSearch`/`ParallelExhaustiveSearch`,
`BM25InvertedFile`, `InvertedFile`) gets its own concrete engine struct, each carrying only
the state that kind actually needs. There is no enum tag or string name anywhere in this
hierarchy — the concrete Julia type itself is what `add_item!`, `search_live`,
`restore_engine`, and every other generic function dispatch on.

```{mermaid}
classDiagram
    class AbstractSearchEngine {
        <<abstract>>
    }
    class SearchGraphEngine {
        index: SearchGraph
        ctx: SearchGraphContext
        minrecall: Union~Nothing, Float32~
        opt_beamsearch: OptBeamSearch
        search_ctx_pool: ContextPool
        deleted_ids: Set~UInt32~
        lock: ReadWriteLock
    }
    class GenericEngine~IndexType~ {
        index: IndexType
        ctx: Any
        search_ctx_pool: ContextPool
        deleted_ids: Set~UInt32~
        lock: ReadWriteLock
    }
    class BM25Engine {
        index: Union~Nothing, BM25InvertedFile~
        voc: Union~Nothing, Vocabulary~
        model: Nothing
        ctx: InvertedFileContext
        search_ctx_pool: ContextPool
        deleted_ids: Set~UInt32~
        lock: ReadWriteLock
    }
    class InvertedFileEngine {
        index: Union~Nothing, InvertedFile~
        voc: Union~Nothing, Vocabulary~
        model: Union~Nothing, VectorModel~
        distance: PreMetric
        ctx: InvertedFileContext
        search_ctx_pool: ContextPool
        deleted_ids: Set~UInt32~
        lock: ReadWriteLock
    }
    AbstractSearchEngine <|-- SearchGraphEngine
    AbstractSearchEngine <|-- GenericEngine
    AbstractSearchEngine <|-- BM25Engine
    AbstractSearchEngine <|-- InvertedFileEngine
```

A few design choices worth calling out:

- `GenericEngine{IndexType}` covers `ExhaustiveSearch`/`ParallelExhaustiveSearch` (and any
  future dense index with no engine-specific state) with a single struct parameterized by
  the wrapped index type, instead of one struct per index kind.
- `minrecall`/`opt_beamsearch` only exist on `SearchGraphEngine` — only a `SearchGraph`
  autotunes a `BeamSearch` toward a target recall.
- `BM25Engine` and `InvertedFileEngine` are both left untrained (`index === nothing`,
  `voc === nothing`) until `index!(engine, corpus)` is called explicitly, exactly once,
  with a real corpus, since both index kinds need a `Vocabulary` before they can be
  constructed at all — `BM25Engine` never needs a `model` (it scores from raw
  bags-of-words), so that field is always `nothing` there, kept only so every text engine
  shares the same shape. There is no implicit auto-training on a project's first
  `append_items!` batch anymore: `add_item!` on an untrained text engine errors outright.
- Every kind shares three fields regardless of what else it carries: `deleted_ids::Set{UInt32}`
  (logically deleted document ids — `UInt32` uniformly, matching the id type search
  results actually come back as), `lock::ReadWriteLock`, and `search_ctx_pool::ContextPool`
  (see below).

## Staging vs. indexing: only a `SearchGraph` has the split

`append_items!`/`add_item!` on a `GenericEngine`/`BM25Engine`/`InvertedFileEngine` index
synchronously — an item is searchable the moment the call returns, exactly as before. A
`SearchGraphEngine` is the one exception: `SimilaritySearch.jl`'s own `SearchGraph`
separates *staging* raw vectors into its database from the (expensive) graph-connection
work, so this package exposes that same split instead of hiding it:

- `insert_dense!(index::SearchGraph, ctx, item) = push_item!(index.db, item)` only ever
  appends `item` to `index.db` — cheap, and durable the instant it happens (see
  Persistence below), but `index.adj` (the graph itself) is untouched.
- `IndexEngine.index!(engine::SearchGraphEngine)` is the explicit, idempotent step that
  actually builds graph connections for whatever has been staged since the last call (or
  since creation) — it delegates to `SimilaritySearch.index!(engine.index, engine.ctx)`,
  which itself only ever processes the backlog (`length(engine.index)+1:length(database(engine.index))`),
  so calling it repeatedly, or with nothing new staged, is a cheap no-op.

`search_live`/`allknn`/`fft`/`closestpairs`/`bichromatic_kclosestpairs` only ever see
items `index!` has actually processed — staging alone is not enough. This decouples *when*
an item becomes durable (immediately, on `append_items!`) from *when* it becomes
searchable (only after an explicit `index!`), so a caller controls when the expensive
graph-connection cost is paid — once per big batch, on a schedule, or right before the
next round of queries — instead of paying it synchronously on every single insert the way
every other engine kind still does.

## Concurrency model

None of the four underlying index kinds tolerates a search running concurrently with an
insertion into the *same* index — a search reading `index.adj`/`index.db` while
`add_item!` resizes/appends to those same arrays is exactly the kind of concurrent
read-during-mutation none of them are built for. But all four *do* safely support running
multiple searches concurrently against the same index, since that is exactly what their
own `searchbatch`/`allknn` parallel paths already rely on internally.

### `ReadWriteLock`

Each engine's `lock` is a custom reader/writer lock (built from a `Threads.Condition` plus
a reader count), not a plain `ReentrantLock`: `search_live`/`current_beamsearch` take it as
a *read* lock (any number of readers concurrently), while `add_item!`/`index!`/
`mark_deleted!`/`calibrate!` take it as a *write* lock (exclusive of every reader and every
other writer).

```{mermaid}
sequenceDiagram
    participant S1 as search_live (thread 1)
    participant S2 as search_live (thread 2)
    participant W as add_item! (thread 3)
    participant L as engine.lock

    S1->>L: read_lock (readers 0 to 1)
    S2->>L: read_lock (readers 1 to 2)
    Note over S1,S2: both searches run concurrently
    W->>L: write_lock (blocks: readers > 0)
    S1->>L: release (readers 2 to 1)
    S2->>L: release (readers 1 to 0)
    L->>W: write lock granted
    Note over W: insert_dense! / push_item! using engine.ctx
    W->>L: release
```

A read-to-write "upgrade" on the same logical operation would deadlock (the write lock
waits for the reader count to hit zero, including the reader this same call is itself
holding) — so a `SearchGraphEngine`'s `minrecall`-driven auto-`calibrate!` inside
`search_live` is always resolved *before* the read lock is acquired, never nested inside
it.

### `ContextPool`

Guarding the index data isn't enough by itself: `SearchGraphContext`/`GenericContext`/
`InvertedFileContext` are all *mutable, reused* scratch spaces (beam buffers,
visited-vertices state, per-batch cost counters, ...), and two concurrent searches sharing
the same context object corrupt each other's scratch state — confirmed directly by a
segfault inside `SearchGraph`'s own beam search when two threads raced on a shared
context.

`ContextPool` avoids both bad alternatives — sharing one context (unsafe) and allocating a
fresh one on every single call (wasteful, since these contexts are non-trivial to
allocate) — by handing each concurrent `search_live` call its own checked-out context,
returned to the pool when done:

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    A["search_live call"] --> B{"pool.available<br/>non-empty?"}
    B -- yes --> C["pop! an idle context"]
    B -- no --> D["deepcopy(pool.template)"]
    C --> E["run the search with this context"]
    D --> E
    E --> F["checkin!: push! back onto pool.available"]
```

The pool grows lazily to (and then stays at) however many concurrent searches an engine
has actually seen at once — never pre-allocated speculatively, never shrunk either. `ctx`
itself (the engine's own field) is never touched by `search_live`; it stays reserved for
insertion, which already runs under an exclusive `write_lock`, so sharing it there is
safe.

## Persistence: one storage unit per concern

Earlier iterations of this design re-serialized the *entire* engine state — including the
whole index — on every mutation. The current design instead gives each kind of state its
own RocksDB column family (or, for a `SearchGraph`'s raw vectors, its own file outside
RocksDB entirely — see below), so a mutation only ever rewrites the storage it actually
touched.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
    subgraph db["one RocksDB directory per project"]
        records[("records<br/><small>_id → MetadataRecord (fixed shape)</small>")]
        meta[("meta<br/><small>_id → free-form meta (JSON)</small>")]
        oplog[("op_log")]
        idxkw[("idx_keywords<br/><small>keyword → _ids</small>")]
        idxrefs[("idx_refs<br/><small>referenced doc_id → _ids</small>")]
        engine[("engine <small>(ENGINE_CF)</small><br/><small>one key per engine struct field</small>")]
        adj[("searchgraph_adj <small>(ADJACENCY_CF)</small><br/><small>object_id → direct neighbors</small>")]
        sparsedb[("sparse_db <small>(INVFILE_DB_CF)</small><br/><small>append-only raw object blocks</small>")]
    end
    mmapfile[["dense_vectors.mmapdb<br/><small>-- not RocksDB --<br/>one row per staged vector</small>"]]

    ProjectManager -- "put_metadata! / get_metadata" --> records
    ProjectManager -- "get_meta / get_raw_meta" --> meta
    ProjectManager -- "secondary lookups" --> idxkw
    ProjectManager -- "secondary lookups" --> idxrefs
    EngineStore -- "save_field! / load_field" --> engine
    AdjacencyStore -- "save_neighbors! / load_neighbors" --> adj
    InvertedFileObjectStore -- "append_objects! / load_object_blocks" --> sparsedb
    append_items_dense["append_items!<br/>(SearchGraph only)"] --> mmapfile
```

Every RocksDB column family above lives in the *same* directory/connection as the
project's metadata store (`Project.ProjectManager.db`) — `Project.open_project`'s
`extra_cf_names` keyword is how `IndexEngine`'s persistence layer gets its own column
families listed alongside `Project`'s, since every column family that exists on disk must
be named at `opendb` time on *every* open, not only the first. `dense_vectors.mmapdb` is
the one exception: a plain file, alongside (not inside) the RocksDB directory.

### `EngineStore`: per-field keys, not one blob

`EngineStore` is a `field_name::Symbol => value` map, one RocksDB key per struct field.
`save_field!`/`load_field` touch exactly one key; `save_fields!` is only used for rare,
one-shot multi-field transitions (right after `create_engine`, or the moment a text
engine's vocabulary is first trained). A soft delete only ever rewrites `:deleted_ids`; a
`calibrate!` call only ever rewrites `:opt_beamsearch`.

### Dense vectors: a memory-mapped file, not a RocksDB column family

A `SearchGraphEngine`'s raw vectors are fixed-dimension `Float32` data — exactly what
`SimilaritySearch.MMapMatrixDatabase` is for, and its own append-only counter/growth/fsync
discipline already gives durable, in-order, crash-safe storage with no need for
RocksDB's batch-keying scheme, at a much cheaper per-vector read than a RocksDB point
lookup (confirmed empirically against `VectorDatabase`/`BlockMatrixDatabase` in
`SimilaritySearch.jl`'s own test suite). `append_items!` writes staged vectors directly
into this file, at stage time — not through `CallbackLog` at all, unlike everything else
in this section — since a vector is durable-worthy the moment it's staged, long before any
graph-linking work happens. The file (`dense_vectors.mmapdb`) is created lazily, on the
first dense append, since its dimension isn't known before then.

Batch size matters a lot here: `MMapMatrixDatabase` `fsync`s once per `append_items!`
call, never per individual vector, so the number of calls a caller makes (not the total
vector count) drives wall-clock time — confirmed empirically, 200,000 128-dim vectors as
one 200,000-item call took ~0.10s; the same total split into calls of 10 items took
~2.1s; one call per single item measured roughly 1000x slower than the all-at-once case.
Prefer fewer, larger `append_items!` calls over many small ones.

### Incremental adjacency/posting-list persistence: different shapes, by necessity

The graph/posting-list structure itself is the other expensive, ever-growing part, so it
is never saved as a single value either. Its incremental format is driven by
`IndexEngine.CallbackLog`, an `AbstractLog` backend that fires a `flush(index, sp, ep)`
callback on every `:add!` event a mutating call reports — `SimilaritySearch.jl`
standardizes every index kind's `LOG` calls onto this one event name for a real structural
mutation, regardless of which entry point triggered it, so `CallbackLog` never has to
branch on the event itself. What *does* differ by index kind is the *shape* of what gets
saved, and *when* this callback fires relative to `append_items!`.

```{mermaid}
sequenceDiagram
    participant Caller as index!(handle)
    participant Idx as SearchGraph
    participant CB as CallbackLog
    participant ES as EngineStore
    participant AS as AdjacencyStore

    Note over Caller,Idx: append_items! already staged vectors into<br/>dense_vectors.mmapdb -- no CallbackLog involved
    Caller->>Idx: SimilaritySearch.index!(engine.index, ctx)
    Idx->>Idx: build graph connections for the staged backlog (range sp:ep)
    Idx->>CB: LOG(:add!, index, ctx, sp, ep)
    Note right of Idx: fires BEFORE connect_reverse_links!<br/>index.adj[sp:ep] holds only direct links
    CB->>AS: save_neighbors!(i, direct_neighbors(i)) for i in sp:ep
    CB->>ES: save_field!(:graph_len, ep)
    Idx->>Idx: connect_reverse_links! (in memory only)
```

For a `SearchGraph`, `LOG` fires *before* `connect_reverse_links!` runs for that range —
so what's captured at that instant is exactly the direct-links-only slice. This is by
design, not a bug to route around: `connect_reverse_links!` isn't idempotent (re-running
it on an already-complete graph would duplicate reverse edges), so the on-disk format
never saves reverse links at all. `:graph_len` (how far graph-indexing actually got,
which can lag behind how many vectors are staged in `dense_vectors.mmapdb` if the process
closed between an `append_items!` and its follow-up `index!`) lets reloading resume
exactly where indexing left off, over the same, already-fully-restored `.db`.

`BM25InvertedFile`/`InvertedFile` have no direct/reverse-link hazard: their own `LOG` only
fires after a call's mutation is fully done, so `InvertedFileObjectStore` simply appends
the raw objects just inserted (`invertedfile_objects`) as a new block — and unlike
`SearchGraph`, they have no staging step at all: `append_items!` indexes them
synchronously, right away. Reloading rebuilds the whole index by replaying every saved
object back through the library's own `push_item!` — a rebuild-by-reinsertion design, not
a real on-disk posting-list format. This is a deliberate scaling limit, not an oversight:
it's fine up to a few million documents, since the whole corpus and the whole rebuilt
index have to fit in memory and reloading costs the full original indexing time again. It
is *not* a design for billion-document corpora, which need genuinely disk-backed,
paged-on-demand posting lists.

`GenericEngine` (`ExhaustiveSearch`/`ParallelExhaustiveSearch`) has no incremental format
of its own — its `on_change` just flags `pending_flush[]`, and `embedded.jl` saves the
*whole* index as a single `:index` value right after the triggering `add_item!` call
returns. This is acceptable for these exact, in-memory-only index kinds, which have no
adjacency or posting-list structure to split apart in the first place, and index
synchronously on every `add_item!` same as the text engines.

### Reopening a project

```{mermaid}
sequenceDiagram
    participant Caller as open_project
    participant MM as dense_vectors.mmapdb
    participant ES as EngineStore
    participant AS as AdjacencyStore
    participant IE as IndexEngine

    Caller->>ES: load_field(:kind)
    Caller->>MM: open_dense_vectors(dir) → vector_blocks (one block, every staged vector)
    Caller->>AS: load_neighbors(i) for i in 1:graph_len
    Caller->>ES: load_field(:graph_len, 0)
    Caller->>IE: build_searchgraph(distance, vector_blocks, load_neighbors, graph_len)
    IE->>IE: replay every staged vector into index.db (in full)
    IE->>IE: add! each of the first graph_len objects' saved direct neighbors
    IE->>IE: connect_reverse_links! once, over 1:graph_len
    IE-->>Caller: reconstructed SearchGraph -- index.len[] = graph_len
    Caller->>IE: restore_engine(state, on_change) → SearchGraphEngine
```

`graph_len` can be `<= length(index.db)`: every staged vector is always fully restored
into `.db` (that's durable from the moment it was staged), but only the first `graph_len`
of them were ever graph-indexed before the project last closed — if it closed between an
`append_items!` and its follow-up `index!` call, the gap is restored as staged-but-not-yet-
searchable, waiting on a future `index!(handle)` call to catch it up, exactly as it was
before closing.

`restore_engine` dispatches on `state.kind` exactly the way `create_engine` dispatches on
an index type — `IndexEngine.extra_state_fields(kind)` gives the static, per-kind list of
which extra `EngineStore` keys to read back (`:minrecall`/`:opt_beamsearch` for a
`SearchGraphEngine`, `:voc` for a `BM25Engine`, `:voc`/`:model`/`:distance` for an
`InvertedFileEngine`) before an engine instance exists to ask `snapshot_state` directly.

## Logging: informative output and persistence are independent

Every engine's context installs a logger (`ctx.logger`), fanned out via `LogList` when
more than one backend is active:

- **`InformativeLog`** (from `SimilaritySearch.jl` itself) — always on, prints a throttled
  status line to `stderr`. Purely informative.
- **`FileLog`** — the same throttled status line, but to any caller-given `IO` (an open
  file handle, or `stdout`/`stderr`) instead of a hardcoded `stderr`. Also purely
  informative: adding one changes nothing about what gets persisted.
- **`CallbackLog`** — the mechanism described above: forwards every report, untouched by
  its own throttling, to whatever `on_change` closure `embedded.jl` installed (the actual
  persistence trigger).

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    Event["LOG :add! event<br/>(from push_item!/append_items!)"] --> LogList
    LogList --> InformativeLog["InformativeLog<br/>→ stderr, throttled"]
    LogList --> FileLog["FileLog<br/>→ any IO, throttled<br/>(optional)"]
    LogList --> CallbackLog["CallbackLog<br/>→ on_change(index, sp, ep)<br/>(persistence trigger)"]
```

`FileLog`/`InformativeLog` and `CallbackLog` are independent by construction: removing
either informative logger changes nothing about persistence, and vice versa.

## Soft deletes

`mark_deleted!` adds a document's id to `deleted_ids` and nothing else — the underlying
index is never touched, so no rebuild or backfill is needed. `search_live` reports a
`deleted` flag per candidate instead of silently dropping deleted candidates and
backfilling with the next-best live one: compensating for deletions by overfetching would
have to grow with the total number of deletions, and it would hide from the caller which
ids were even considered. A caller that wants `k` *live* results after filtering is
expected to page for more (e.g. via a cursor over successive top-`k'` windows) at a layer
above this one — `SimilaritySearchServer`, not this package.

## Whole-dataset operations

`allknn`, `fft`, `closestpairs`, and `bichromatic_kclosestpairs` all run synchronously,
in-process, directly against a dense project's index — no job queue, unlike the HTTP
API's `POST /api/v1/jobs/allknn`. Each does real work proportional to the *whole* dataset
(or two datasets, for the bichromatic case): `allknn` is every item's own top-`k`
neighbors at once; `fft` (Farthest-First-Traversal) picks `k` well-separated items for
diverse sampling; `closestpairs` finds the `k` globally closest pairs within one project
(near-duplicate/echo detection); `bichromatic_kclosestpairs` finds the `k` closest pairs
between a project's own index and a second, unindexed collection of vectors. All four
require a dense (`SearchGraphEngine`) project that's had `index!` run at least once — none
apply to a text project.

## Where this leaves `SimilaritySearchServer`

This package covers project lifecycle, core CRUD, calibration, and the whole-dataset
operations above. Pagination policy over soft-deleted results, HTTP/CLI surfaces, job
queues, and telemetry all live one layer up, in the sibling `SimilaritySearchServer`
package, which depends on this one and is kept in sync with it as this package's design
settles.
